standard_prerequisites.name: In a local domain of dimension one the maximal ideal is the radical of a principal ideal generated by any nonzero element of it
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 33758-33759, where a nonzero pi in the maximal ideal is fixed and m = sqrt((pi)) is recorded
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the dimension-one hypothesis into the valuation-like statement that an element of the fraction field with a pole can be written as pi to a negative power times an element of A, which is what produces the integer m with P'(alpha)^{-1} = pi^{-m} a.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Taylor expansion of a polynomial in two variables, P(x + y) = P(x) + P'(x) y + R(x, y) y^2 for some R in A[x, y]
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: recorded at proof lines 33763-33766 and used again at proof lines 33792-33796
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the quadratic error term that makes the Newton correction work modulo the next power of the maximal ideal.

standard_prerequisites.name: Completeness of a local ring with respect to its maximal-adic filtration: a sequence whose consecutive differences lie in higher and higher powers of the maximal ideal converges, and its limit can be used in A
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof line 33774, where beta is defined as the limit of the constructed sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the inductively constructed sequence into an actual element beta of A with the required congruence beta - alpha in m_A^c.

core_obligations: Turn the dimension-one hypothesis on the complete local domain A into a usable valuation statement: fix a nonzero pi in the maximal ideal so that m = sqrt((pi)), write P'(alpha)^{-1} = pi^{-m} a with m at least 0 and a in A, then replace c by a value at least m + 1 and choose n with m_A^n contained in (pi^{c + m}) (proof lines 33758-33762).

Set up the approximation scheme: record the Taylor expansion P(x + y) = P(x) + P'(x) y + R(x, y) y^2 and announce a sequence alpha_m, alpha_{m+1}, alpha_{m+2}, ... with the three properties alpha_k congruent to alpha modulo pi^c, alpha_{k+1} - alpha_k in (pi^k), and (P + Q)(alpha_k) in (pi^{m + k}); the desired root beta is the limit of that sequence, which exists by completeness (proof lines 33763-33774).

Base case: because the coefficients of Q lie in (pi^{c + m}), the value (P + Q)(alpha) lies in (pi^{c + m}), so alpha_m = alpha satisfies the third property and the first property propagates to every later index (proof lines 33776-33780).

Induction step: write alpha_{k+1} = alpha_k + delta and compare both summands of (P + Q)(alpha_k + delta) with their values at alpha_k, using that Q(alpha_k + delta) agrees with Q(alpha_k) modulo pi^{c + m + k} and that P'(alpha_k) agrees with P'(alpha) modulo (pi^{m + 1}); recombining gives (P + Q)(alpha_{k+1}) congruent to (P + Q)(alpha_k) + P'(alpha) delta modulo pi^{k + m + 1} (proof lines 33782-33807).

Choose the correction explicitly as delta = -P'(alpha)^{-1} (P + Q)(alpha_k) = -pi^{-m} a (P + Q)(alpha_k), check that this delta lies in (pi^k) by the induction hypothesis, and conclude that the sequence can be continued one step further (proof lines 33808-33810).
proof_roadmap: Fix pi with m = sqrt((pi)) and absorb the inverse of P'(alpha) into a negative power of pi, raising c so that c is at least m + 1 and choosing n with m_A^n inside (pi^{c + m}) (proof lines 33758-33762).

Build a sequence alpha_k approximating alpha, with consecutive differences in (pi^k) and (P + Q)(alpha_k) in (pi^{m + k}), starting from alpha_m = alpha; take beta to be its limit (proof lines 33763-33780).

In the induction step use the Taylor expansion and the congruence P'(alpha_k) = P'(alpha) modulo (pi^{m + 1}) to show that the Newton correction delta = -P'(alpha)^{-1}(P + Q)(alpha_k) lies in (pi^k), which closes the induction (proof lines 33782-33810).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is Krasner's lemma in the discretely valued case, stated for a complete local domain A of dimension one rather than for a complete field: for a polynomial P over A with a root alpha that is not a root of the derivative, every perturbation of the coefficients inside a sufficiently high power m_A^n of the maximal ideal produces a root beta of the perturbed polynomial with beta - alpha inside any prescribed m_A^c (statement lines 33749-33754). The proof is a Newton approximation that has to be run over a ring rather than a field, so the first move is to convert the dimension-one hypothesis into the statement that the maximal ideal is the radical of a principal ideal, which allows the inverse of P'(alpha) to be written as pi^{-m} a and fixes the two exponents c and n relative to each other (proof lines 33758-33762). The construction is an explicit sequence alpha_k with three simultaneous properties, whose limit is the required root; the induction step compares both summands of (P + Q)(alpha_k + delta) with their values at alpha_k through the Taylor expansion and through the congruence P'(alpha_k) equal to P'(alpha) modulo (pi^{m + 1}), yielding the explicit correction delta = -pi^{-m} a (P + Q)(alpha_k) and the verification that it lies in (pi^k) (proof lines 33782-33810). The argument consumes no cited result at all: the only inputs are the structure of a one-dimensional local domain, the Taylor expansion of a polynomial, and completeness of A.
